content: 1. Mujtar El V Muñoz N, Cormick BPM, Pullemann M, and Tittonell P discussed the role and management of soil biodiversity in ensuring food security and nutrition. Their work was published in Global Food Security in 2019, highlighting the current state of knowledge in this area. 2. The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and the World Health Organization (WHO) jointly published a report in 2019 on sustainable healthy diets, emphasizing the importance of integrating health and sustainability into dietary guidelines. 3. Johnston JL, Fanzo JC, and Cogill BC conducted a descriptive analysis in 2014 to understand the determinants and processes influencing sustainable diets and their impacts on health, food security, and environmental sustainability. This was published in Advances in Nutrition. 4. Swinburn BA, Kraak VI, Allender S, and colleagues authored the Lancet Commission Report in 2019, addressing the global syndemic of obesity, undernutrition, and climate change, and proposing integrated solutions to tackle these interconnected challenges. 5. Hunter D, Özkan I, Moura de Oliveira Beltrame D, and others explored whether the environment is conducive to leveraging biodiversity for improved nutrition. Their findings were published in Frontiers in Nutrition in 2016. 6. Lartey A, in 2015, advocated for linking agriculture with nutrition under Sustainable Development Goal 2 (SDG 2), emphasizing the importance of dietary diversity indicators. This work was published by the Emergency Nutrition Network. 7. Remans R, Attwood S, Bailey A, and Weise S proposed an Agro-biodiversity Index to measure sustainability in food systems. Their work was included in the 2017 publication Mainstreaming Agro-biodiversity in Sustainable Food Systems by Biodiversity International. 8. The 2020 publication Biodiversity, Food, and Nutrition: A New Agenda for Sustainable Food Systems by Routledge highlighted the critical role of biodiversity in achieving sustainable food systems. 9. Harary AJ, Boushey CJ, Pollard CM, and colleagues developed a novel dietary assessment method using a mobile food record to measure healthy and sustainable diets. This methodology was detailed in Nutrients in 2015. 10. Burlingame B, Vogliano C, and Eme PE emphasized the potential of agricultural biodiversity in promoting sustainable diets, with a focus on Pacific Small Island Developing States. This was discussed in the 2019 Advances in Food Security and Sustainability publication. 11. Mijatovic D, Sakalian M, and Hodgkin T, in 2018, explored the integration of biodiversity into production landscapes, as part of a report by the Global Environment Facility. 12. The 2006 decision of the Conference of the Parties (VIII/23) in Curitiba, Brazil, under the Convention on Biological Diversity, addressed the importance of biodiversity conservation for sustainable development. 13. Norström AV, Cvitanovic C, West S, and colleagues outlined principles for knowledge co-production in sustainability research in Nature Sustainability in 2020. 14. Montana J, in 2019, examined the organizational dimensions of global biodiversity expert processes and their implications for co-production in sustainability science, as published in Sustainability Science. 15. Johns T, Smith IF, and Eyzaguirre PB, in 2006, explored the links between agriculture and health in a report by the International Food Policy Research Institute. 16. Rüegg SR, Nielsen LR, Buttigieg SC, and others proposed a systems approach to evaluate One Health initiatives in Frontiers in Veterinary Science in 2018. 17. Hahn T, Olsson P, Folke C, and Johansson K, in 2006, discussed the role of bridging organizations in adaptive co-management of wetland landscapes in Sweden, as published in Human Ecology. 18. The World Health Organization (WHO) published a report in 2014 on gender, climate change, and health, emphasizing the intersection of these critical issues. 19. WHO also released guidance in 2014 on protecting health from climate change through health adaptation planning. 20. Tandon N, in 2013, highlighted opportunities for advancing women’s sustainable livelihoods, food security, and climate resilience in the Caribbean Small Island Developing States (SIDS) in a working paper by the International Policy Centre for Inclusive Growth. 21. WHO’s 2017 report on double-duty actions for nutrition emphasized strategies to address both undernutrition and obesity simultaneously. 22. The International Food Policy Research Institute (IFPRI) published a 2015 report on the role of agriculture in improving nutrition and health outcomes. 23. Fanzo J edited the 2013 book Diversifying Food and Diets, which explored the role of biodiversity in improving nutrition and food security. 24. The 2003 WHO/FAO report on diet, nutrition, and the prevention of chronic diseases provided comprehensive guidelines for addressing non-communicable diseases through dietary interventions. 25. Alae-Carew C, Nicoleau S, Bird FA, and colleagues conducted a systematic review in 2020 on the impact of environmental changes on the yield and nutritional quality of fruits, nuts, and seeds, published in Environmental Research Letters. 26. Gomez San Juan M, Bogdanski A, and Dubois O, in 2019, discussed pathways toward a sustainable bioeconomy in a report by the FAO. 27. The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) published a 2011 report on transitioning toward a green economy, emphasizing sustainable resource use. 28. Bringezu S, in 2019, proposed science-based targets for global sustainable resource use in Resources. 29. Palmer MA and Febria CM, in 2012, described the critical role of ecosystems in maintaining environmental health in Science. 30. The 2018 Global Bioeconomy Summit Communiqué emphasized the importance of bioeconomy strategies for sustainable development. 31. Contento IR, in 2008, linked research, theory, and practice in nutrition education in the Asia Pacific Journal of Clinical Nutrition. 32. Hunter D, Borelli T, Beltrame DMO, and others, in 2019, highlighted the potential of neglected and underutilized species for improving diets and nutrition in Planta. 33. Jabbar MA, Peden DG, Mohamed Saleem MA, and Li Pun H edited a 2000 report on agro-ecosystems, natural resource management, and human health in East Africa, published by the International Livestock Research Institute. 34. Catley A, Alders RG, and Wood JLN, in 2011, reviewed participatory epidemiology approaches in The Veterinary Journal. 35. Bagnol B, in 2012, advocated for addressing gender issues as a sustainable way to control Newcastle Disease in village chickens, as part of the International Network for Family Poultry Development. 36. Jibril AH, Umoh JU, Kabir J, and colleagues applied participatory epidemiology techniques to investigate Newcastle Disease among rural farmers in Nigeria, as published in The Journal of Applied Poultry Research in 2015. 37. Azhar M, Lubis AS, Siregar ES, and others, in 2010, described participatory disease surveillance and response in Indonesia to control avian influenza in Avian Diseases. 38. Fanzo J and Davis C, in 2019, explored whether diets can be healthy, sustainable, and equitable in Current Obesity Reports. 39. The FAO’s 2017 report on nutrition-sensitive agriculture and food systems provided practical guidance for integrating nutrition into agricultural practices. 40. Payne CL, Scarborough P, and Cobiac L conducted a systematic review in 2016 on the relationship between low-carbon-emission diets, nutritional quality, and health outcomes, published in Public Health Nutrition. 41. The World Resources Institute (WRI) published the World Resources Report: Creating a Sustainable Food Future in 2018, synthesizing strategies for sustainable food systems. 42. Blesh J, Hoey L, Jones AD, and colleagues, in 2019, examined the role of agroecology in sustainable food systems in World Development. 43. Fan S, in 2019, highlighted the growing urgency to address the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in food policy, as reported by IFPRI. 44. Springmann M, Clark M, Mason-D’Croz D, and others, in 2018, explored options for keeping the food system within environmental limits in Nature. 45. Medawar E, Huhn S, Villringer A, and Witte AV conducted a systematic review in 2019 on the effects of plant-based diets on the body and brain, published in Translational Psychiatry. 46. Zmora N, Suez J, and Elinav E, in 2019, reviewed the relationship between diet, health, and the gut microbiota in Nature Reviews Gastroenterology & Hepatology. 47. The InterAcademy Partnership’s 2018 report outlined opportunities for future research and innovation in food and nutrition security and agriculture. 48. Thies E, in 2000, discussed the potential of underutilized species and crops for sustainable agriculture in a report by Deutsche Gesellschaft für Technische Zusammenarbeit (GTZ). 49. Foyer CH, Lam H-M, Nguyen HT, and others, in 2016, highlighted the consequences of neglecting legumes for human health and sustainable food production in Nature Plants. 50. Khoury CK, Bjorkman AD, Dempewolf H, and colleagues, in 2014, examined the increasing homogeneity in global food supplies and its implications for food security in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences USA. 51. Negri V, in 2012, discussed policies supporting on-farm conservation of neglected and underutilized species in the context of climate change, as part of a Biodiversity International conference. 52. The 2017 Global Land Outlook by the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification addressed sustainable land management strategies. 53. Sachs J, Schmidt-Traub G, Kroll C, and others, in 2017, published the SDG Index and Dashboard Report, providing a comprehensive assessment of progress toward the Sustainable Development Goals. 54. Hunter D, de Souza Dias B, Borelli T, and others, in 2020, emphasized the inclusion of food systems, biodiversity, nutrition, and dietary health in the Post-2020 Global Biodiversity Framework, as part of a joint submission by the Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT.
